terms.comment: Priscian’s term: verbum trānsitīvum. The older grammarians called such verbs āctīva (Charisius, Diomedes; Lewis & Short s.v. āctīvus).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 249.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
